analysis.title: Is it all Just a Handful of AI Giants? Assessing the Breadth of S&P 500 Earnings and Returns
key_insights: Goldman Sachs Investment Strategy Group (ISG) argues S&P 500 earnings and returns are broad-based, not driven only by a handful of AI giants. This responds to a WSJ article from October 24, 2026 saying two AI chipmakers make up 34% of the earnings boom.
The median S&P 500 company is growing earnings at a low-double-digit rate this year. That is above the 6.5% trend earnings growth and the 7.4% annualized actual growth since WWII.

Reported S&P 500 earnings grew 27% in Q1 2026 and 50% in Q2 2026. Both quarters were boosted by one-off gains on two technology companies' equity investments. Excluding those gains, underlying growth was around 20%-30%.
AI spending beneficiaries (72 stocks, 24% of S&P 500 market cap) grew earnings by over 90% and contributed around half of the S&P 500's 28% growth in the first half of 2026.

Underlying earnings growth is positive in all eleven sectors in 2026. Health Care is the only sector with negative headline growth, entirely because of one-time IPR&D charges. Consensus expects positive 2026 growth in all eleven sectors.

About 75% of S&P 500 companies are expected to grow Q3 2026 earnings year over year, so about 25% (132 stocks) are expected to decline. The post-GFC median share of growers is 65%, and Q3 consensus ranks in the 83rd percentile since 2009.
The S&P 500 excluding AI-related companies has returned 12% year to date, the same as the overall index. Returns have come entirely from earnings growth while multiples fell.

S&P 500 forward P/E fell 16%, from 22.0x at the start of 2026 to 18.4x through October 30, 2026. AI spending beneficiaries' multiples fell 38% to 15.3x NTM P/E, a 17% discount to the S&P 500. Both the absolute and relative levels are the lowest since late 2022.

ISG preliminarily expects high-teens US earnings growth in 2027, excluding one-time 2026 gains, outpacing non-US developed and Chinese equities. It maintains its recommendation to stay invested in US equities.

sector_views.rationale: Headline 2026 earnings growth is negative only because of one-time IPR&D charges. Underlying growth excluding those charges is positive.
ISG recommends staying invested in US equities, based on the strength of the US economy and corporate earnings and an expected high-teens 2027 US earnings growth rate.

earnings_insights: Reported S&P 500 earnings growth was 27% in Q1 2026 and 50% in Q2 2026, both boosted by non-recurring equity investment gains at two technology companies. Excluding those gains, underlying growth was about 20%-30%.
FactSet consensus (estimates, not reported) has S&P 500 Q3 2026 and Q4 2026 earnings growth at 28% each, as of October 30, 2026. Q3 reporting is under way.
Q3 2026 consensus expects about 75% of S&P 500 companies to grow earnings year over year, versus a 65% post-GFC median. That is an estimate, not a reported figure.
Median-firm earnings growth is low-double-digit in H1 2026, and is expected at a similar rate in Q3 and Q4 (consensus estimates).
AI spending beneficiaries grew earnings over 90% in H1 2026 (excluding one-off gains) and contributed about half of the S&P 500's 28% H1 growth.

trade_ideas.description: Stay invested in US equities (strategic recommendation, no specific instrument)
trade_ideas.rationale: Anchored by the strength of the US economy and corporate earnings, and ISG's expectation of high-teens US EPS growth in 2027 outpacing non-US developed and Chinese equities.

risk_factors: Forecasts are estimates based on assumptions and are subject to significant revision as economic and market conditions change.
AI spending beneficiaries' multiples have fallen 38% this year, which the report reads as skepticism that such rapid profit growth can last.
About 25% of S&P 500 companies (132 stocks) are expected to report year-over-year earnings declines in Q3 2026.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows S&P 500 quarterly earnings growth as reported: 27% in Q1 2026 and 50% in Q2 2026, with Q3E and Q4E at 28% each. The median firm grows 13% in Q1 and 12% in Q2 2026, and the trend since WWII is 6.5%.
Exhibit 2 shows the share of S&P 500 companies with positive YoY earnings growth at 79% in Q1 2026 and 75% in Q3E, against a historical median of 65%.

Exhibit 3 decomposes 2026 total return into NTM EPS, NTM P/E and dividends for AI spending beneficiaries, hyperscalers, the S&P 500 excluding AI-related companies, the S&P 500 and AI-related companies. The text states the S&P 500 and the S&P 500 excluding AI-related companies both returned 12%.
Exhibit 4 shows EPS growth for China, the UK, Europe ex-UK, the US and Emerging Markets ex-China across Q1 2026, Q2 2026 and the 2026 ISG forecast, plus US growth excluding one-off gains.
vol_and_positioning: Valuation compression: S&P 500 forward P/E fell from 22.0x to 18.4x in 2026. AI spending beneficiaries' multiples fell 38% to 15.3x NTM P/E. ISG reads this as investor skepticism that rapid AI profit growth can last.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings and returns are broad-based. The median company grows at a low-double-digit rate, all eleven sectors show positive underlying growth, and the S&P 500 excluding AI-related companies returned 12%, the same as the index.
tension_points.bear_case: A WSJ article says two AI chipmakers make up 34% of the earnings boom. About 25% of companies (132 stocks) are expected to report Q3 declines, and AI spending beneficiaries contributed around half of H1 earnings growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: ISG says the 75% share of Q3 growers would need to fall below the 65% post-GFC median, and the median-company growth rate would need to drop below the 6.5% trend, to undercut the breadth thesis.

theme_stances.key_argument: Earnings and returns across the S&P 500 remain broad-based, not driven by a handful of AI giants.
theme_stances.evidence: earnings and returns across the S&P 500 remain broad-based

theme_stances.key_argument: The US will provide more stable and reliable earnings growth, supported by structural advantages, and ISG expects high-teens US earnings growth in 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: we maintain our recommendation to stay invested in US equities
